title: 같은 뜻, 다른 느낌: 칭찬일까, 흉일까?
objective: By the end, you can read a short review, comment or conversation and tell whether a word sounds positive, negative, polite or casual. You can also choose the right word from five common pairs.
summary: Learn five pairs of Korean words that mean almost the same thing but feel different: one sounds kind or polite, and the other sounds blunt or negative.
note: The words come in pairs. The first word in each pair usually sounds softer, more polite or more positive.

task.title: Choose the right feeling
task.line: Think about each situation: are you praising or worrying? Is it polite writing or a casual chat? Then choose or write the word that fits.

sections.heading: Five pairs: same meaning, different feeling

items.text: A compliment about a nice body shape.
Often sounds like worry: too thin, maybe not eating well.
items.example: 요즘 많이 말랐네. 밥은 잘 먹어?

items.text: A polite word for low prices, common in writing, ads and reviews.
items.example: 이 식당은 점심 메뉴가 저렴한 편이에요.

items.text: A casual word; sometimes it suggests low quality.
Used only for good smells, like flowers, soap or perfume.
A neutral word; with words like 이상한 or 탄, it means a bad smell.
A good habit of not wasting. 아끼지 않다 means 'to be generous'.
A casual, negative word for a person who does not like to spend or share.
items.example: 우리 사장님은 너무 짜요. 커피 한 잔도 안 사 줘요.

items.text: A soft, respectful way to talk about age.
Blunt; it can hurt when you say it about someone else.
items.example: 늙었다는 말을 들으면 기분이 안 좋아요.

sections.heading: Read: a café review
paragraphs: 회사 근처에 있는 작은 카페예요. 커피 값이 저렴하고, 문을 열고 들어가면 커피 향기가 좋아요. 사장님이 재료를 아끼지 않아서 케이크도 크고 맛있어요. 다만 손님이 많아서 좀 시끄러워요.
The writer likes this café. The words 저렴하다, 향기 and 아끼지 않다 all sound positive. Only the last sentence is a complaint.

sections.heading: Tip: how to choose
paragraphs: Before you choose a word, ask yourself two questions. Am I praising, or am I worried or complaining? Am I writing something polite (an ad, a review, a message to a boss), or chatting with a friend?

Koreans, especially older family members, often talk about weight when they meet you. '많이 말랐네' is usually worry, not a compliment, so don't take it as one. And don't say 늙었어요 about other people. Even as a joke, it can sound rude.

exercises: Choose the word that fits: ① 쓰레기통에서 이상한 (향기 / 냄새)가 나요. ② 친구가 너무 (아껴서 / 짜서) 같이 밥 먹기가 싫어요.
Your friend lost a lot of weight because she was sick. Which word shows that you are worried about her? 너 많이 (날씬해졌네 / 말랐네). 괜찮아?
You are writing an ad for a hotel website. Which word sounds more polite? 저희 호텔은 객실 요금이 (저렴합니다 / 쌉니다).
Read and answer in English. Is 민수 씨 stingy? Why or why not?: 민수 씨는 평소에 돈을 아껴 써요. 그런데 친구 생일 선물에는 돈을 아끼지 않아요.
Rewrite the sentence so it sounds softer. Use 나이가 들다: 저도 이제 늙어서 밤에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
answers: No. He saves money in daily life, but he is generous when he buys his friends' birthday gifts.
저도 이제 나이가 들어서 밤에 잠을 잘 못 자요.
